papers.title: Machine Learning Assisted Design of Complex and High Entropy Alloys by Hybrid HiPIMS/Pulsed-DC PVD Process for Low Carbon Energy Applications in Extreme Environments
papers.summary: Complex and high entropy alloys are attracting much attention currently thanks to their mechanical and corrosion resistance properties in harsh environments, in particular needed for carbon-free energy applications. However, their elaboration in bulk and in thin film form in a trial-and-error approach is impractical due to their complexity and the cocktail effect. The recent development of artificial intelligence brings a new possibility for their elaboration and adjustment of their properties. Firstly, we present an overview of Materials and data science research. Then we describe how DIADEM - French initiative for Materials and Data science convergence - tackles the development of innovative coatings for carbon-free energy applications (nuclear, high temperature electrolysis, ...) thanks to the development of a nationwide network of synthesis and characterization platforms - the DIADEM discovery hub. We describe in particular DIADEM-2D, an AI-driven Hybrid HiPIMS/Pulsed-DC PVD process using 4 cathodes in confocal combinatorial configuration. We present the high entropy alloy determination using data from the literature for corrosion resistance in molten salt media and nuclear accidental conditions. An element-independent model gathering deposition parameters and coating properties has been implemented allowing the design of protective coatings with a particular composition. We demonstrate the feasibility of this process and its accuracy.

papers.title: Visualizing Chiral Edge Modes in Twisted Cuprate Superconductors via Scanning-Probe Quantum Sensing
papers.summary: Recently, unconventional superconductivity hosted by twisted van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures has received immense interest due to the exotic pairing symmetry, electronic interactions and nontrivial topological nature that are naturally relevant to the fast-advancing quantum technologies. Here, we report scanning-probe quantum sensing of nanoscale electromagnetic behaviors of twisted vdW cuprate superconductors. Using single-spin relaxometry, we directly visualize edge modes spontaneously formed in twisted Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x (BSCCO). By investigating temperature dependent variations of edge-state-induced quantum spin relaxation, we experimentally evaluate the magnitude of nontrivial topological band gap opened at nodal points in twisted BSCCO and its critical temperature behaviors under different twist angles. We further observe alternating chiral domains defined by edge modes, exploring experimental signatures of in-plane magnetic field-induced topology in 45{\deg} twisted BSCCO. Our results advance the current understanding of twisted vdW nodal superconductors, presenting an appealing high-temperature topological superconducting material platform for cutting-edge quantum innovation.

papers.title: Laser-induced metastable (anti-)skyrmion states with higher-order topological charge
papers.summary: Ultrafast creation and manipulation of topologically non-trivial spin objects promises significant potential for spintronic applications. Here, we demonstrate laser-induced nucleation of skyrmions and antiskyrmions with topological charge up to $|Q|=3$ from the saturated magnetization state of a Co/Ni-multilayer which does not intrinsically host a skyrmionic ground state. The resulting configuration of spin objects thus constitutes a metastable, thermodynamically hidden magnetic state. We control the number and type of spin objects by the excitation fluence and the external out-of-plane magnetic field.

papers.title: Unmodeled states and uncertain action outcomes in agentic scanning tunneling microscopy
papers.summary: In physical experiments, interventions can alter hidden experimental states in ways that cannot be predicted in advance. Autonomous scientific agents must therefore interpret the consequences of their interventions while operating with incomplete knowledge of the experimental state. Here we investigate this problem using scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) tip conditioning, traditionally a human-expert-intensive task governed by inaccessible tip apex conditions and uncertain action outcomes. We introduce quailbot, an agent harness that places the LLM inside the instrument feedback loop by linking physical interventions with experimental readbacks. After a brief apprenticeship with a human expert, frontier LLM agents autonomously completed end-to-end tip conditioning on an STM and passed an independent verification. The contingencies that arose during the experiments further exposed the limits of LLM agentic autonomy when relevant experimental states or dynamics were hidden or unmodeled. Our results show that future autonomous physical experimentation requires agents to infer hidden and unmodeled experimental states, track the outcomes of their actions, and operate within the observability and action limits of real instruments.

papers.title: Closed analytical form of many-body free volume and thermodynamics of monodisperse hard disks
papers.summary: The hard disk model is a fundamental reference system for excluded volume physics, liquid structure, and 2D ordering. Yet, despite its apparent simplicity, an analytical formulation of its thermodynamics has remained difficult because the free volume available to disks centers has a highly nontrivial many-body geometry. Here we show that this geometry admits a closed and exact representation: for any given hard disk configuration, the free volume can be analytically expressed through intersection areas of up to five exclusion disks. This provides a direct geometrical route from particle coordinates to the configurational partition function and entropy. We prove that the N disk partition function factorizes into a product of conditional free volumes and identify its two limiting asymptotic forms: the low density fluid regime controlled by extensive cavities and the high density fluid regime controlled by intensive private cells. Using the geometric measures computed from representative equilibrium particle configurations, the resulting theory reproduces the established hard disk equation of state over almost the entire density range up to close packing. At intermediate densities, the analysis reveals a mixed fluid regime in which localized caged defects provide an additional configurational entropy within the density interval preceding liquid hexatic coexistence. Finally, the five disk intersection area is shown to be a sensitive local scalar measure of hexagonal ordering, complementing the orientational order parameter and emphasizing the central role of many-body correlations.

papers.title: Full-Continuum Ultrafast Quantum Gas Microscopy
papers.summary: Quantum gas microscopy provides single-shot access to many-body configurations, yet has so far relied on pinning atoms to a discrete lattice during fluorescence readout. Here, we realize ultrafast atom-resolved fluorescence microscopy of an ultracold $^{162}$Dy gas directly in free space, with all external confinement removed during imaging. Exploiting the large mass and broad optical transition of dysprosium together with a high numerical aperture in-vacuum objective, we detect single atoms within $4\,\mu\mathrm{s}$ while maintaining an effective point-spread function with a full width at half maximum of $254.8(3)\,\mathrm{nm}$. We achieve a single-atom conditional classification fidelity of $99.72(3)\%$ for identified fluorescence candidates. We use the measured single-atom response to construct a statistical configuration-inference model that recovers atomic positions and multiplicities, coming from overlapping atoms, directly from single fluorescence snapshots. We further benchmark our reconstruction algorithm through end-to-end Monte Carlo simulations with known ground-truth atomic configurations, obtaining a reconstruction fidelity of $98.7\%$. Our approach, applicable to a wide variety of atomic species, extends quantum gas microscopy beyond predefined detection lattices, enabling atom-resolved measurements of counting statistics and higher-order spatial correlations directly on the intrinsic length scales of continuum many-body systems.

papers.title: Soft elasticity of soft shells
papers.summary: Soft modes of a shell are one-parameter families of non-trivial deformations that preserve the elastic energy. We identify all soft modes of the soft shells described by the variational theory of put forward by Sonnet and Virga (2025). They are seen to be strictly connected with the Bonnet families, a special class of solutions to the problem posited by Bonnet, who asked whether there exist non-trivial isometries that preserve the mean curvature. Differential geometry deems as equivalent all surfaces in one and the same Bonnet family, but continuum mechanics is interested more specifically in soft deformation modes and the shapes they traverse, as they may describe ways to ignite fluctuations of soft shells that ideally require no energy to be activated. We give a general criterion for the existence of soft modes and a method to construct them based on a cascade of path integrations. We apply both criterion and method to some exemplary cases.

papers.title: Framework to identify defect-insensitive electron transport in topological semimetals
papers.summary: Topological semimetals are of increasing interest to replace conventional metals for interconnects in future semiconductor chips, due to their potential to exhibit decreasing resistivity with reducing wire dimensions and a lower sensitivity to electron scattering at defects. First-principles evaluation of promising topological semimetals for interconnects typically employ non-equilibrium Green's functions (NEGF) techniques to estimate defect scattering, but such calculations for specific defect geometries are difficult to systematize and compare between disparate materials. Here, we develop an NEGF-based approach to systematically and rapidly evaluate the defect sensitivity of electron transport in materials without depending on material-specific defect geometries. Specifically, we analyze the eigen-spectrum of the transmission matrix for an incoherent ensemble of all-possible single-atom vacancy defects, which clearly reveals eigenvalues close to 1 for defect-insensitive transport modes. Applied to the leading candidates, we show that this robustness to defect scattering is extremely sensitive to surface orientation and Fermi level for each material. We find nearly-perfect insensitivity to defects only for wavevectors with single transport modes within specific Fermi level ranges in CoSi(001) and PtAl(001). Importantly, we also find high insensitivity for certain non-isolated modes in NbAs that emerge specifically due to spin-orbit coupling; these modes could not be identified previously as they were buried in the total transmission. These non-isolated modes have been buried in previous studies of total transmission, and can now be directly compared to other materials due to our standardization of defect-creation. This technique improves the state-of-the-art NEGF method and enables unbiased evaluation of future topological semimetal candidates for nanoscale interconnects.

papers.title: Contact Renormalization of One-Mode Electron Correlation: Validation in Four- and Ten-Electron Systems
papers.summary: A stationary many-electron eigenstate has one dynamical phase although its internal response can be strongly multimode. We ask whether the stationary Hartree--Fock information carrier contains enough information to determine the scalar correlation energy through one effective return. In regularized Hartree--Fock, Gaussian primitive products fix a minimum-information relative-coordinate mode before any one-mode reduction; virial completion defines the correlation source, while exact contact measures the additional return restriction created by neighboring occupied pairs. The Be-like $1s^22s^2$ sequence establishes the one-valence-pair boundary: with no neighboring occupied valence pair, the source returns through the universal floor $D_0=\sqrt{1+\delta^2}$. Ten-electron molecules and Ne-like ions then test how finite-pair contact dresses that return. The same parameter-free source--return construction reproduces the established molecular and ionic correlation trends with quantitative accuracy. The numerical agreement therefore serves as validation of a physical separation between source strength and return restriction, rather than as the objective by itself.

papers.title: Asset-Normalized Distribution Reliability Budget Optimization Using Historical Outage Benefits and Work-Type Learning
papers.summary: Reliability investments compete for constrained capital but are often evaluated in separate programs. This paper presents a data-driven framework that translates historical work orders, geographic asset records, outage events, and costs into comparable customer-minute and customer-interruption benefits at the circuit-zone level. A normalization process maps historical device names and non-isolating assets to current automaticisolating-device zones and links investments to pre- and postconstruction outage histories. Utility data covering more than $250 million in investments completed from 2010 to 2020 are used to estimate benefit factors for seven work types. Those factors feed a mixed-integer portfolio model that selects at most one applicable action per zone under a capital budget. Observed reductions range from 32% to 94% for customer-minutes interrupted and from 43% to 93% for customer interruptions. The framework provides a traceable path from heterogeneous utility records to zone-level reliability investment decisions

papers.title: DRAMA-Eval: A Benchmark for Context-Aware, Multi-Turn, Multi-Speaker Speech Generation
papers.summary: Recent advances in speech generation are shifting toward context-aware, multi-turn, and multi-speaker synthesis. While these capabilities are in high demand for applications such as audiobook and audio drama production, evaluation has not kept pace with these advances. Beyond traditional zero-shot Text-to-Speech (TTS), modern systems in this domain primarily fall into three categories: instruction-controllable generation models, multi-turn dialogue models, and the audio branches of audio-visual generation models. However, existing benchmarks evaluate these paradigms in isolation, failing to provide a unified assessment of context modeling, instruction following, and multi-speaker generation. Meanwhile, recent progress in audio understanding models has made it feasible to evaluate such complex scenarios using LLM-as-a-Judge approaches. To bridge this gap, we introduce DRAMA-Eval, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating such systems. DRAMA-Eval utilizes structured script contexts and offers a holistic evaluation framework covering objective, local, and global aspects of generation quality, enabling the assessment of acoustic fidelity, sentence-level execution, and long-range coherence. We benchmark leading open-source and commercial models on a human?verified dataset. The results reveal critical weaknesses in long-range speaker consistency and implicit instruction following that require deep contextual understanding. To facilitate reproducible research, we release a 12-hour bilingual (Chinese-English) test set of manually corrected real-world scripts, accompanied by ground-truth audio, evaluation code, and benchmark results.

papers.title: Exposing Noise-Deficiency Signatures of Deep Learning-Based False Data Injection Attacks Through AC State Estimation
papers.summary: Deep learning (DL)-based false data injection (FDI) attacks can resemble normal measurements and evade both conventional bad data detection (BDD) and measurement-space data-driven detectors. This paper identifies a previously overlooked signature of such attacks in state-estimation (SE) residual space. The residuals of reconstruction-based DL attacks exhibit deficient stochastic variation, manifested as abnormally small residual energy and reduced directional dispersion. We establish the conditions under which this signature emerges and explain why the attacks carrying it can evade conventional BDD. We show that SE can reveal residual-space differences obscured by operating-state variation in measurement space. We then explain the origin of the signature through the noise-suppression mechanism of DL attack generation. A generator can learn the reproducible structure of historical measurements but cannot reproduce stochastic measurement components that are unpredictable from its input. This signature enables label-free detection using a simple two-sided test on the conventional BDD statistic, while the full residual vector can also be exploited when labeled attack samples are available. Experiments on the IEEE 14-bus and 118-bus AC systems show that the label-free test detects up to 99% of three representative DL attacks at a false-alarm rate comparable to that of BDD, which detects at most 5%. Ablation studies further examine the effects of residual representation, decision rule, and measurement-noise magnitude and distribution.

papers.title: Resource Slicing for Time-Sensitive Data Traffic in Non-Terrestrial Networks with FSO ISLs
papers.summary: In multi-hop Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks, time-sensitive packets experience queueing across multiple satellite hops, causing per-hop waiting times that accumulate and make the maximum end-to-end (E2E) delay difficult to guarantee. This paper presents a novel multi-hop slicing framework that reserves time-frequency resources for each time-sensitive flow of data originating at each satellite, aiming to maintain the reservation of communication resources along every inter-satellite link (ISL) on its route to the ground station (GS). The number of time-frequency resource blocks (RBs) reserved per-hop is determined from the data packet arrival statistics, E2E delay budget, and target level of reliability. Reservations on consecutive links are temporally aligned to enable pipelined forwarding of the time-sensitive data flows aggregated from terrestrial user terminals on the different LEO satellites. We evaluate the proposed framework against conventional scheduling and resource-allocation baselines, including pure time-division multiple access (Pure-TDMA), first-in-first-out (FIFO), and farthest-satellite-first (FSF), over the same multi-hop LEO satellite path. Under light traffic conditions, the baseline schemes provide comparable delay performance; however, their high-percentile delays increase sharply as data traffic load grows, whereas the proposed framework exhibits substantially slower delay growth. At the high arrival rate and high reliability target considered, the proposed scheme requires about 31 ms, a factor of 2.5-6.8 lower than the 76, 180, and 210 ms required by FIFO, FSF, and Pure-TDMA.

papers.title: A graph decomposition approach for the synthesis of EMPs in directed acyclic networks
papers.summary: This paper considers the identifiability of dynamical networks whose topology is a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG), in the context where not all nodes are excited and not all nodes are measured. The objective is to construct a valid and parsimonious Excitation and Measurement Pattern (EMP), i.e. a selection of excited and measured nodes, that allows to identify the whole network with a small number of excitations and measurements. We show first that a DAG can be decomposed into a set of trees and parallel paths networks. We propose an algorithm that achieves this decomposition and computes an EMP that combines EMPs for the individual trees and parallel paths networks. papers.title: Model-Free Generative Stealthy Attacks on Safety-Critical Vehicle Cyber-Physical Systems
papers.summary: Existing stealthy attacks presuppose white- or grey-box access to the target system, unrealistic in practice. We establish a certified residual-impact bound and an observable stealth budget around a stealth-consistent anchor, and show that recurrence and context conditioning are structural necessities for closed-loop, multivariate cyber-physical systems (CPS). The resulting attack generator, trained against a Wasserstein critic under a stealth-constrained impact objective, induces a hazardous 2.51 m lane departure while evading five intrusion detection systems, and, in real-time hardware-in-the-loop tests, a speed deviation of approximately 8 km/h while staying below the detection threshold. papers.title: On Sample Complexity Bounds for Frequency-Domain System Identification
papers.summary: We study the sample complexity of frequency-domain system identification with bounded measurement noise. We focus on interpolatory identification algorithms, which return models consistent with both the data and a priori constraints. For equally spaced samples, we sharpen previous worst-case bounds on the consistency-set radius. Its excess above the noise level decays as $N^{-2}$, where $N$ is the number of samples, and a matching lower bound shows that this rate is tight. We then examine whether bounded stochastic noise allows identification below the noise level. We show that high-probability error bounds can converge to zero. Their convergence rate depends on how strongly the noise distribution is concentrated near the boundary of the noise set. For example, noise uniformly distributed on a disk gives an upper bound of order $(\log N/N)^{2/3}$. Numerical experiments examine these convergence rates and the effect of the noise distribution on the identification error.

papers.title: Practical Complete Tracking Through Gimbaled Unidirectional Actuation with Application to Multirotor UAVs
papers.summary: This paper addresses the problem of practical tracking control for robotic vehicles with gimbaled unidirectional actuators, with special application to multirotor unmanned aerial vehicles. A widely recognized obstacle to tracking control for multirotors is the free-fall singularity --- when a multirotor is commanded to free fall, the vehicle's target attitude becomes undefined. This singularity is a pathology pertinent to all robotic vehicles with gimbaled unidirectional actuators. This paper considers the general theoretical problem for vehicles with gimbaled actuators. Starting from a baseline robust controller that assumes unconstrained inputs, we redesign the control law to be compatible with the gimbaled actuator. This is accomplished by driving the output of the gimbaled actuator to a ball centered at the target input value. The baseline controller's tracking guarantees are recovered in a practical sense. We apply our results to synthesize a global practical complete position tracking controller for multirotor unmanned aerial vehicles. The theory is demonstrated in simulation.

papers.title: Scalable Reservoir Computing for Disturbance Localization and Identification in Power Grids
papers.summary: In this paper, we present a novel method for the localization and temporal waveform reconstruction of disturbances in complex power grids using observations of system state variables. Although various methods exist for detecting these events, accurately identifying and responding to them remains a significant challenge due to the grid's size, speed, complexity, and inherently dynamic behavior. We formulate a method for disturbance localization and reconstruction based on reservoir computing, a recurrent neural network architecture. We show that our method is able to recover the time dependence of previously unobserved disturbances, is robust to missing information, and can operate online. The approach requires only observed system data and knowledge of the network topology, without requiring a physical model of the system dynamics, and can recover simultaneous disturbances occurring at multiple locations. We implement a scalable parallelized reservoir architecture and demonstrate our algorithm on test IEEE cases and a reduced WECC system.

papers.title: Pinching Antenna Systems (PASS): Principles, Positioning and Opportunities
papers.summary: Pinching-antenna systems (PASS) have garnered significant attention owing to their ability to enhance the capacity and coverage of wireless networks by guiding electromagnetic waves through waveguides before radiation. As such, PASS are regarded as promising enabling technologies for sixth-generation (6G) communication networks. In this paper, we present a comprehensive survey of the state of the art in PASS, covering operating principles, positioning methodologies, performance evaluation, resource allocation, and the application of artificial intelligence (AI) to PASS-enhanced wireless networks. We first introduce the fundamental principles of PASS from both materials and physics perspectives. Building on this foundation, we present positioning methodologies for both the user side and the base station side. We then evaluate the communication performance of PASS in both uplink and downlink scenarios under different blockage models. Furthermore, we systematically review existing designs for PASS-enhanced wireless networks from a performance optimization perspective. Finally, we survey research efforts that leverage AI to address challenges in dynamic and complex scenarios.

papers.title: Stability Enhancement of Cascaded DC Systems via Source Output-Impedance Reshaping Using Model-Free Control
papers.summary: Cascaded DC systems may become unstable through source-load impedance interactions even when their constituent converters are locally stable. This paper proposes a source-side model-free control (MFC) method that reuses bus-voltage feedback to reshape the source output impedance while preserving nominal reference-to-output dynamics. The controller uses only nominal source-loop information and requires neither a load-converter model nor load-side measurements. A current-controlled buck source supplying a regulated buck-resistor load that exhibits constant-power load (CPL) behaviour at low frequencies is used as the case study. Impedance analysis predicts that the proposed MFC increases the maximum stable load power by approximately 50%, thereby improving the stability margin of the cascaded system. Switched-model simulations confirm preservation of the nominal reference-to-output response and show that the MFC-controlled system remains stable at load levels for which the baseline system becomes unstable.

papers.title: QoE-Driven Hybrid Resource Allocation for Multi-User OFDMA Semantic Communications
papers.summary: In this paper, we develop a quality-of-experience (QoE)-driven hybrid resource allocation framework for multi-user downlink orthogonal frequency-division multiple access semantic communication systems, where the hybrid framework jointly handles continuous and discrete decision variables. Specifically, we formulate a mixed continuous-discrete optimization problem to jointly optimize transmit power, subcarrier allocation, and semantic decisions under coupled power and spectrum constraints. To better characterize semantic service quality, we propose a preference-inverse multiplicative exponential QoE that is bounded and non-compensatory, capturing the intrinsic ``both-required'' property of semantic rate and similarity. To solve the optimization problem, we develop a projection-based multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient framework that enforces feasibility for continuous and discrete actions. Furthermore, we integrate Gumbel-softmax relaxation with an adaptive performance-driven temperature annealing scheme to enhance the learning of discrete semantic decisions. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed framework achieves superior convergence, greater stability, and higher QoE compared to the conventional QoE design and penalty-based or fixed-temperature baselines, highlighting the benefits of our QoE design and the effectiveness of hybrid decision learning in semantic communications.

papers.title: Model-Free Output-Admittance Reshaping for Stability Enhancement of Grid-Connected Inverters
papers.summary: Grid-connected inverters can be unstable when their current-control loops interact with an uncertain external network. Returning the existing controller to improve damping also alters current tracking because tracking dynamics and output admittance are coupled. This paper adds a local model-free control (MFC) loop around the existing current controller to reduce output admittance while closely preserving nominal current-tracking dynamics. The added loop uses local inverter parameters without an external grid or neighbouring converter model. A Norton formulation separates reference tracking from the current response to terminal-voltage disturbances and establishes a tracking-preservation condition for admittance reshaping. Reducing the disturbance response makes the inverter behave more like an ideal controlled current source. Averaged-model simulations show reductions exceeding 65% in the magnitudes of all four dq output-admittance elements over 10-200 Hz, with closely preserved current-tracking dynamics. Generalised Nyquist analysis predicts small-signal stability for all sampled grid-impedance cases with MFC, compared with 90.0% without MFC.

papers.title: Resilience in Wireless: A Lyapunov-Constrained Integrated Sensing, Communication, and Control Approach
papers.summary: Traditional wireless networks mainly use reliability metrics to evaluate network stability. However, reliable data delivery alone cannot fully characterize network stability under variations in wireless environments and physical tasks. Wireless network resilience provides a broader perspective by describing the ability to maintain acceptable service and recover from disruptions. We develop an integrated sensing, communication, and control (ISCC) framework that incorporates communication reliability and sensing error into a state-dependent Lyapunov constraint for adaptive BS beamforming. The resulting transmit-power minimization problem is non-convex and solved via semidefinite relaxation and successive convex approximation with rank-one recovery. We establish conditional mean-square ultimate boundedness, while simulations demonstrate improved resilience and faster recovery over a static baseline.

papers.title: NECTAR: Automatic Negative Clue Estimation via Centroid-Space Mapping for Target Speaker Extraction
papers.summary: Target speaker extraction (TSE) aims to extract a desired speaker from a mixture using auxiliary clues such as enrollment speech. An interferer-related representation can provide a useful negative clue for TSE, but such information is not directly available from the target enrollment. To derive this representation from the observed mixture, we analyze the relationship between the speaker representations of a speech mixture and its constituent speakers. Our analysis shows that the mixture centroid lies near the midpoint of its constituent speaker centroids, whereas this relationship does not hold for single-utterance embeddings. Based on this observation, we propose NECTAR, NEgative Clue for TARget speaker extraction, which automatically derives an interferer-related negative clue from the mixture using the centroid-space relationship. We further introduce a Centroid-Space Mapper (CSM) to estimate the required centroid representations from a mixture and a target enrollment. NECTAR achieves the highest SI-SDRi on Libri2Mix among the compared systems trained on LibriSpeech train-clean-100, reaching 16.18 dB.

papers.title: An exploration of plug-and-play flow matching for full-waveform inversion on breast imaging
papers.summary: Full-waveform inversion (FWI) reconstructs sound-speed fields from measured waveforms, by solving an optimization problem that minimizes the discrepancy between measured waveforms and those predicted by a numerical wave-propagation model. However, choosing suitable regularization for this optimization is challenging because it must stabilize the inversion while preserving relevant structures, prompting us to investigate whether priors learned from representative sound-speed images can improve reconstruction. In this work, we adapt plug-and-play flow matching (PnP-Flow) to FWI by alternating waveform-misfit updates with updates from a pretrained flow prior. We explore the effectiveness of PnP-Flow reconstruction by comparing it with total-variation (TV) regularization using noiseless transmission-only plane-wave data. Separate flow priors are trained on two circular-inclusion model families with constant and spatially varying backgrounds. We evaluate the method both on these in-distribution circle models and under substantial distribution shift by transferring the Gaussian-circle prior and reconstruction settings to breast phantom patches without retraining or retuning. Using the same number of waveform-misfit updates, the proposed PnP-Flow framework generally improves circle reconstruction accuracy and recovers breast lesion contrast more accurately than TV baselines.

papers.title: SURE-Tagger: Structured Speech Representations for Compositional Evaluation and Targeted Data Selection
papers.summary: Speech conveys linguistic content, speaker characteristics, temporal interactions, paralinguistic cues, and acoustic environments. While recent speech captioning models describe these dimensions in natural language, inconsistent attribute coverage and ambiguous omissions hinder systematic analysis across recordings. We introduce SURE-Tagger, a framework that constructs semi-structured speech representations with explicit attribute values, supplementary descriptions, and abstention under insufficient evidence. By integrating specialist observations through language-model reasoning, SURE-Tagger enables speech conditions to be consistently identified and jointly queried across datasets. We further introduce Tag-Bench, combining real recordings with controlled, agentically synthesized speech scenes and verified attribute annotations. On Tag-Bench, SURE-Tagger achieves the highest scores on 25 of 29 evaluated dimensions for real speech and 24 of 29 for synthetic speech, outperforming caption-based baselines across structural and descriptive attributes. Beyond annotation, we use these representations to construct cross-dataset evaluation subsets and reveal condition-specific ASR errors. Using a separate candidate pool, SURE-Tagger-guided selection reduces the overall ASR error rate of Qwen3-ASR-1.7B by 14.3% relative to the unadapted model under a one-hour fine-tuning budget, while caption-guided and random selection increase error in the same setting. These results demonstrate how structured speech representations can connect rich annotation, compositional evaluation, and targeted model improvement.

papers.title: Melody Guidance for Audio Diffusion Models Without Retraining
papers.summary: Controlling melody in audio generation normally requires training a conditional generative model on audio paired with pitch curves or MIDI notes. We instead guide an existing unconditional diffusion model, originally trained without melody inputs, to follow a target melody without retraining or modifying it. During inference, a differentiable pitch detector steers the sampled audio toward the desired pitches, while the diffusion model keeps it close to the distribution of realistic audio learned during training. Our main contribution is a sampling method that balances these two directions, providing melody control while preserving audio quality. To improve stability, we initialize sampling with a simple synthesized version of the target melody rather than pure noise. Experiments on piano, guitar, and singing voice show melody accuracy comparable to conditional models trained specifically for melody control. Our method therefore adds melody control to existing audio diffusion models without requiring paired melody data or task-specific retraining.

papers.title: Quadrotor Guidance for Tasks along Elliptical Boundary
papers.summary: This paper presents a guidance method that enables a quadrotor uncrewed aerial vehicle to perform inspection tasks along an elliptical boundary enclosing a structure of interest. The proposed guidance approach leverages a bifurcation theory-based framework that supports multiple inspection tasks, including convergence to a desired viewpoint, switching between viewpoints along the boundary, constant-speed elliptical circumnavigation, and circumnavigation with sectorial dwell-time constraint. Stability analysis of the proposed guidance dynamics establishes convergence of the generated reference trajectories to the desired behavior. The control parameters in the proposed method further allow the settling time of the reference trajectory to be specified for each task. The resulting reference velocity expressions are closed-form and algebraically simple, facilitating practical implementation. A qualitative comparison with existing guidance methods highlights the flexibility of the proposed approach in achieving different inspection tasks through a unified framework, while relying on simpler guidance computations. The proposed guidance method is validated through numerical simulations using a six-degree-of-freedom quadrotor model with model uncertainties, and a cascaded sliding-mode controller that tracks the generated reference trajectories under bounded disturbances.

papers.title: Decision Timescales in Max-Pressure Traffic Signal Control: Theory, Methodology, and Validation
papers.summary: Max-pressure (MP) control adapts signal phases to prevailing traffic states, but its decision timescale is typically fixed a priori. This paper treats the decision timescale as an explicit dimension of MP control. We first characterize the trade-off between responsiveness and switching efficiency by quantifying how an equivalent switching loss reduces service capacity over a finite decision interval. This yields a load-dependent critical timescale determined by switching loss and normalized traffic load, together with a performance-oriented operating range above the stability boundary. Building on this result, we propose Variable-Timescale Max-Pressure (VT-MP), in which each intersection selects its decision interval according to local operating conditions, allowing the control timescale to vary across time and space. We establish strong stability of the resulting asynchronous heterogeneous controller under uniformly admissible local loads and bounded decision intervals, and introduce a downstream receiving-supply correction for finite-storage implementation. Three experiments provide mechanism validation and network-level evaluation. A single-intersection experiment confirms that the preferred decision interval increases systematically with traffic load and follows the derived characteristic timescales. In a store-and-forward network, heterogeneous VT-MP reduces total queueing time by 31.0% relative to the best fixed-interval benchmark. In a microscopic 5x5 SUMO network, it reduces mean trip delay by 24.3%, from 213.3 s to 161.5 s, and peak network accumulation by 12.3%. These findings show that the MP decision timescale should be treated as a traffic-state-dependent control variable rather than a fixed implementation parameter.

papers.title: Regret-Based Max-Pressure Traffic Signal Control under Uncertain Traffic States
papers.summary: Max-pressure (MP) traffic signal control selects phases using pressure scores computed from estimated traffic states, but these states are uncertain and their consequences depend on whether they alter phase ranking and how much pressure is lost. This paper develops a decision-oriented Regret-Based Max-Pressure framework that represents uncertainty through phase-selection regret, defined as the pressure loss of a candidate phase relative to the pressure-maximizing phase under each plausible latent state. We propose Stochastic Regret MP, which minimizes expected regret under a calibrated residual distribution, and Distributionally Robust (DR) Regret MP, which minimizes worst-case expected regret over a Wasserstein ambiguity set. Robustifying regret rather than absolute pressure makes the formulation invariant to state-dependent pressure components shared by all candidate phases, thereby focusing robustness on relative phase quality. We further derive an explicit queue-linear pressure-loss bound and establish strong queue stability when the net-service reserve exceeds the resulting loss coefficient. Numerical experiments show that both methods reduce normalized true-state pressure regret by about 70% relative to Point-estimate MP, while DR Regret MP yields lower network queues than direct robustification of absolute pressure. In microscopic SUMO experiments on a 28-intersection real-world network, Stochastic Regret MP and DR Regret MP reduce mean delay by 18.9% and 14.9%, respectively, and retain benefits under detector undercount and failure. The results show that representing uncertainty through its decision consequences can improve reliable traffic control under imperfect state information.

papers.title: Type-based Over-the-Air Computation
papers.summary: Over-the-air computation (OAC) exploits the superposition property of wireless channels to compute functions of distributed data, reducing the communication overhead associated with its multiple access. However, existing OAC frameworks are often designed around specific classes of functions, limiting their applicability to more general nonlinear computations. This paper investigates type-based multiple access (TBMA) as a general framework for OAC, enabling the receiver to recover a histogram of the distributed observations and compute a broad class of functions without modifying the underlying communication scheme. We formulate TBMA as a histogram estimation problem and propose two digital detectors. We prove that a low-complexity successive cancellation algorithm achieves the optimal maximum-likelihood (ML) performance. We derive analytical expressions for the mean squared error (MSE) and compare TBMA with conventional schemes in terms of computation accuracy, transmission duration, bandwidth and energy consumption. Numerical experiments validate the analytical results and demonstrate that, unlike existing OAC techniques, TBMA exhibits an exponential MSE decay with increasing signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and constant transmit energy, independently of the function being computed. These findings position TBMA as a step toward more versatile OAC architectures, compatible with existing transmission schemes, and broadening the range of functions that can be computed directly over the wireless channel and enabling new possibilities for distributed computation and decision-making.

papers.title: A Robust Control Architecture for Multirate Systems and their Interconnections
papers.summary: We introduce a framework for analyzing and designing linear multirate control systems and their interconnections through the lens of robust control. Further, we develop a compositional approach for analyzing interconnections of multirate systems based on individual dissipativity properties. The theoretical conditions can be verified via linear matrix inequalities and they require weak assumptions on the sampling rates, allowing for asynchronous and time-varying sampling rates with or without separated time scales. The practicality of the framework is demonstrated with numerical examples.

papers.title: Do LLM-derived text features improve electricity price forecasts beyond document activity? Evidence from Australia's National Electricity Market
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) can turn market notices and news into features for electricity price forecasting. Such features also record when documents arrive and whether their extraction failed, so a gain measured against a model without text can reflect document activity as well as content. We add the counts of the same documents and of their failed extractions to a no-text LightGBM model and measure each LLM representation against this activity reference, which needs no additional LLM requests. With gpt-6-luna as the extractor, we forecast Australian electricity prices from operator notices (5-30 minutes ahead) and WattClarity news (day-ahead) after the extractor's documented knowledge cutoff, averaging forecasts over three training seeds. For news, the counts alone lower mean absolute error (MAE) by 3.0%, most of the 3.6% reduction that the better LLM representation achieves relative to the no-text model; its increment beyond the counts is not significant. For notices, two of the three LLM representations lower MAE beyond the counts, by 0.14-0.21% and 0.45-0.52%, whether the counts are cumulative or cover recent windows, whereas the third shows no significant reduction. Time-shifted placebos give mixed evidence on whether these gains require text aligned with the target. Benchmarks using the operator's pre-dispatch forecasts (notices) or price history alone (news) are more accurate than all these text models. Gains against the no-text model and the activity reference differ in sign at individual seeds and, for notices with cumulative counts, in seed-averaged forecasts. Text gains should be reported against both references.

papers.title: Channel orthogonalization via movable antennas
papers.summary: This paper investigates the orthogonalization of far-field multiuser channels through the optimal positioning of the antennas constituting an array. To solve the ensuing continuous geometry optimization problem, a graph-theoretic framework is introduced that maps pairwise user channel correlations to graph edges, translating channel orthogonalization into a discrete graph-covering problem on a complete graph. The minimum number of array antennas required for orthogonalization is established for 1D, 2D, and 3D array geometries, and a binary linear program is formulated that identifies the most compact array attaining such orthogonality. The graph framework is also shown to accommodate null-steering scenarios and multipath channels. Furthermore, a fundamental tradeoff is revealed whereby relaxing exact orthogonality to near-orthogonality reduces the antenna count at the expense of a less compact array, and a method is presented to enforce minimum antenna spacings without sacrificing orthogonality.

papers.title: Iterative Behavioral Identification for Covert Misappropriation Attacks
papers.summary: We present a data-driven, three-phase framework for covert misappropriation attacks on closed-loop networked control systems. A man-in-the-middle (MITM) adversary, with access only to intercepted input-output data, incrementally identifies the plant's behavioral subspace while maintaining stealth under an infinity-norm intrusion-detection system (IDS). Phase 1 collects an initial rank-deficient Hankel matrix using a low-amplitude probing signal that satisfies an analytical stealth bound. Phase 2 adapts online rank-increasing experiment design to the closed-loop setting, using causal predictor-based masking to limit IDS residuals while the Hankel rank grows from 1 to the full behavioral rank n + mL in exactly n + mL - 1 steps. We show that the identified subspaces are strictly nested and that the projection error of any desired trajectory decreases monotonically, strictly so almost surely at each rank increase. Phase 3 employs the final Hankel matrix in a DeePC-style optimization to synthesize a covert attack that tracks an arbitrary reference while respecting the IDS constraint. Simulations on a DC motor with PI control demonstrate full-rank identification and stealthy tracking. Stealth is guaranteed analytically in Phases 1 and 3 and is numerically supported in Phase 2. The method is model-free and assumes noise-free LTI dynamics.

papers.title: Automated Fetal Magnetocardiography Reconstruction Using a Biophysical Forward Model
papers.summary: Objective: Fetal magnetocardiography (fMCG) enables early detection of cardiac disease by non-invasively measuring fetal electrophysiological activity. However, current signal estimation methods for fMCG require complex, labor-intensive human processing because they rely on blind source separation or template-based projection techniques. Methods: We propose an automated signal reconstruction approach that recovers fetal and maternal cardiac activity from fMCG measurements without manual annotation. Our approach leverages the relationship between measurements and cardiac signals via a biophysically grounded forward model that represents cardiac sources as time-varying magnetic dipoles. This enables reconstruction of physiologically interpretable three-dimensional vectorcardiographic signals along with their spatial position. Results: Validation on synthetic data with known ground truth confirms accurate recovery of cardiac source parameters. On real fMCG recordings, the reconstruction shows strong agreement with established reference methods. Conclusion: The proposed forward-model approach automatically reconstructs fetal and maternal cardiac activity from fMCG recordings and produces signals in an interpretable vectorcardiographic source domain. Significance: Automated, interpretable fMCG reconstruction could make fetal cardiac assessment more reliable and support potential translation into prenatal care.

papers.title: Foundation Models Meet Power Grid Topology for Cascade Prediction
papers.summary: Accurate early-stage prediction of cascading failure severity is essential for assessing the vulnerability of power transmission networks. However, existing data-driven approaches often rely on network-specific representations, limiting their generalizability across power system topologies. This work investigates the complementary capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for cascading failure severity prediction. First, standalone LLM predictors are developed using a LoRA-fine-tuned LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct model with varying degrees of topological information. A hybrid Graph-LLM fusion framework is then proposed, integrating a Topology-Aware Graph Attention Transformer (TAGAT) with the LLM through confidence-gated fusion. TAGAT captures structural dependencies among transmission lines, while the LLM extracts representations from early-stage power-flow observations and aggregated cascade descriptors. The frameworks are evaluated on 30,000 simulated cascading failure scenarios for each of the IEEE 118-bus and IEEE 300-bus systems. Using only the first four cascade steps, the hybrid framework achieves weighted F1 scores of 0.94 and 0.92, respectively. In cross-system transfer from IEEE 118-bus to IEEE 300-bus, it achieves 0.72 zero-shot accuracy, improving to 0.83 with limited target-system calibration, outperforming standalone models and conventional baselines. These results show the potential of combining graph-based structural learning with foundation models to improve cascading failure severity prediction and cross-system transferability.

papers.title: Density control of large-scale multi-agent systems via tuning of agent interactions
papers.summary: Collective behavior in biological systems emerges through adaptive interactions among units, enabling large populations to coordinate without centralized control. This mechanism raises the question of whether collective behavior in engineered multi-agent systems can likewise be regulated by modifying the interaction law between agents, rather than by directly controlling individual units. To answer this question, we consider large-scale multi-agent systems evolving on a ring and treat the interaction kernel as a time-varying control variable whose evolution regulates the collective dynamics. Using a mean-field formulation, we develop a framework for the analysis and design of kernel-based controllers. We derive explicit conditions for controllability in application-relevant scenarios, and synthesize a state-feedback controller to regulate the kernel dynamics, validated on the microscopic, discrete dynamics. Numerical simulations demonstrate the approach's effectiveness and robustness to unmodeled perturbations. This work constitutes a first step in the design of bio-inspired control strategies for large-scale multi-agent systems by modulation of interactions between agents.

papers.title: Trust-Region Benders for Scalable Multiperiod Expansion Planning for Transmission and Storage
papers.summary: Transmission expansion planning (TEP) seeks to identify cost-effective investment strategies that enable power systems to reliably meet future demand, while accounting for the location, timing, and operational impacts of infrastructure upgrades. As demand grows and renewable penetration increases, there is growing interest in jointly modeling energy storage investments to enhance operational flexibility. This work presents a multiperiod formulation that co-optimizes transmission reconductoring and energy storage installation across multiple planning periods. To solve the resulting large-scale problem efficiently, a Benders decomposition with per-period trust-region stabilization and a relaxation-based warm-start procedure is proposed. The approach is demonstrated on a 2,000-bus Texas system, producing an investment plan spanning 2030-2045 with optimality gap below 1.0%, and is compared against a rolling-horizon approach to highlight the benefits of multiperiod coordination.

papers.title: Reducing 6G Energy Consumption: TDD-Aligned Drain Voltage Modulation for Power Amplifiers
papers.summary: The Power Amplifier (PA) of a base station operates inefficiently at partial load, where back-off from the peak output power wastes supply headroom. Adapting the PA drain voltage to the instantaneous signal recovers this loss but requires frequent switching, increasing hardware cost. We propose TDD-Aligned Drain Voltage Modulation (TDD-DVM), a drain voltage modulation scheme that instead selects the drain voltage level once per Time-Division Duplex (TDD) period based on the downlink resource load and switches the voltage during the uplink window. This is enabled by the authors' previous work on POLITE link adaptation, which spreads the transmit power over resources left unused at partial load and moves the PA into a regime where a lower drain voltage suffices. In a 3GPP Urban Macro system-level simulation across traffic loads, we compare TDD-DVM against baseline approaches under conventional and POLITE link adaptation. At equal delivered throughput, TDD-DVM with POLITE keeps the packet failure ratio of the full drain voltage while consuming up to 35% less power than it under conventional link adaptation and up to 7% less than it under POLITE, roughly half of the gain of an idealized reference.

papers.title: Classical, Machine Learning, and Hybrid Solvers for Partial Differential Equations: An Evidence-Weighted Review and Decision Framework
papers.summary: Machine learning for partial differential equations raises a practical question: when are classical, learned, or hybrid solvers justified? This survey compares the three families in a decision framework organized by data availability, query volume, and certification needs. An amortization law, tested on parametric Darcy flow, shows that surrogates trained on solver-generated data break even only after many queries, beyond thirty thousand for errors below one percent. An evidence ladder, a benchmark reanalysis, and three case studies show that claims of speedup and generalization carry the weakest evidence. Solver choice should follow regime, query volume, and evidence quality, not method novelty.

papers.title: CoupleFlow: Null-Calibrated Auditory Attention Decoding With Time-Locked Brain-Speech Coupling and Flow-Matching Likelihood Ratios
papers.summary: Auditory attention decoding (AAD) seeks to identify the attended talker from brief noninvasive brain recordings by comparing neural responses with competing speech streams. Recent electroencephalography (EEG) decoders report nearly perfect accuracy from one second of data, yet we show that this performance fails to generalize to unseen speech because models exploit trial leakage, eye gaze, and acoustic cues instead of speech evoked neural activity. We introduce CoupleFlow, which decodes attention through temporal coupling between neural and acoustic embeddings. Its predictions remain at chance when the brain signal contains no informative coupling, preventing shortcuts based on speech content or talker identity. A conditional flow matching head implements a likelihood ratio decision rule based on pointwise mutual information between brain and speech. This rule is Bayes optimal when the recording depends only on the attended talker and removes preferences for speech that is likely a priori. We evaluate CoupleFlow with content disjoint splits recovered from the audio and null tests that distinguish genuine temporal coupling from trial recognition. Across nine EEG and magnetoencephalography (MEG) datasets processed through a common pipeline, spanning four languages, high density EEG recordings, listeners with hearing impairment, and a room with multiple talkers, CoupleFlow outperforms linear and deep baselines while all null tests remain at chance. Finally, we derive an evidence accumulation law that predicts accuracy across window lengths from a single parameter per dataset and predicts that parameter from the strength of neural speech tracking. This law identifies recording signal to noise ratio as a limit on decoding speed and reliability and estimates the window length required to reach a target accuracy.

papers.title: Low-Complexity Wideband Channel Estimation for ISAC in Analog Millimeter-Wave Systems
papers.summary: Accurate wideband channel estimation is a key enabler for millimeter-wave (mmWave) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. In the narrowband scenario, the Transformed Spatial Domain Channel Estimation (TSDCE) method was previously shown to provide fast and accurate angle estimation with substantially lower complexity than conventional compressed-sensing approaches based on orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP). However, wideband ISAC scenarios additionally require delay estimation, making joint angle-delay sparse recovery computationally expensive due to the multidimensional dictionary search. In this paper, we propose a wideband extension of TSDCE, namely TSDCE-TD, which incorporates time-domain support and decouples angle and delay estimation. Two variations are proposed for delay estimation: TSDCE-TD (Dict), which uses a one-dimensional delay dictionary, and TSDCE-TD (FFT), which applies Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) zero-padding interpolation. Path estimates are iteratively refined through successive interference cancellation and alternating angle-delay updates. Simulation results show that the proposed methods outperform OMP-based baselines under practical dictionary sizes, while achieving comparable performance at high-resolution settings with substantially lower computational complexity. Moreover, the angle-delay estimates obtained using the proposed approach enable accurate single-anchor indoor localization in a ray-traced environment, achieving sub-20 cm positioning errors and satisfying practical indoor positioning requirements.

papers.title: SEMAC: Spherical Energy Matching Ambisonics Codec for Efficient Higher-Order Ambisonics Compression
papers.summary: Higher-order Ambisonics (HOA) is an attractive format for immersive spatial audio, but its high channel count and directional properties present significant audio coding challenges. The widely deployed Opus audio codec supports HOA through Channel Mapping Families 2 and 3 (RFC 8486), which code and transmit every Ambisonics channel, so the bitrate grows quadratically with the spherical harmonic order. We introduce SEMAC, which instead represents an Ambisonics signal by a quantized full-order directional energy envelope together with fewer CELT-coded transport channels. CELT separates a per-band energy envelope from the signal shape and restores it after quantization, and SEMAC generalizes this principle to directional signals. Since the reduced transport spans only a lower-dimensional subspace, the decoder re-imposes the envelope observed at the encoder input, restoring the directional energy distribution at full order. A MUSHRA test on fifth-order material compares SEMAC against Opus CMF~3 in matched configurations at 512 and 768 kbit/s. SEMAC with 16 of 36 transport channels is rated above full-order CMF~3 at both rates, and at equal transport channel count above order truncation. The proposed SEMAC strategy of coding fewer transport channels with the directional envelope is found perceptually preferable to coding all HOA channels at low precision.

papers.title: When Do Self-Supervised Representations Help Speech Restoration?
papers.summary: Self-supervised learning (SSL) representations are widely used in speech restoration (SR), and the prevailing trend is SSL feature cleansing: fine-tuning the SSL to recover clean features from degraded speech, then conditioning the restoration model on them. However, the representational capability of SSL when encoding degraded speech has been underexplored, and we ask whether cleansing always benefits SR training. Across SSL encoders and perceptual quality proxies, we discover perceptual correlation collapse---under severe degradation, cleansing degraded SSL features toward clean ones misaligns with the SR objective. We hypothesize the restoration backbone can supply the SSL with clues to resolve this collapse, since its intermediate layers already produce partially restored features. We therefore propose Early Restoration Injection (ERI), which routes intermediate features from the restoration backbone into the SSL through a lightweight conditioning network. ERI excels over the unconditioned baseline and, on the VoiceFixer benchmark, achieves competitive performance among multiple baselines.

papers.title: Silence Is Not Assurance: When Production Lane Keeping Assist Does Not Warn, and What It Costs
papers.summary: Production lane keeping assist (LKA) systems tell the driver whether they detect the lane markings, but whether this displayed status reflects what the system perceives, and what happens when it does not, has not been examined in real-world driving. This study introduces CANDID-LKA, a CAN-based Diagnosis of the Indicated Detection status in LKA. It evaluates a proprietary driver-facing status using three signals: the displayed status and the steering torque of the driver, both recorded from the controller area network (CAN) bus of the vehicle, and the lane perception confidence of a third-party vision system observing the same road. The framework examines how the status responds to driving conditions and estimates how completely it reports degraded lane perception by comparing it with the other two signals in a latent-class model. We apply it to 39,800 seconds of real-world driving from 13 vehicle models of three manufacturers. The results show that the status does not respond consistently to the conditions that make markings harder to see, and that the three makes differ widely in how often they report not detected. The latent-class model shows that the displayed status is incomplete: it reports only 47% of degraded seconds as not detected, compared with 80% for the third-party low perception confidence, and in half of the low-confidence episodes it never reports not detected. In the silent seconds in which the status reads detected while the perception confidence is low and the driver is not in control, the standard deviation of lateral position over the next 3 s is about 60% larger than when the status and the perception confidence agree. A detected status thus does not guarantee reliable lane perception, and silence with the driver not in control is the case that most needs attention.

papers.title: Strengthening AC optimal power flow relaxation through offline bound tightening and linear approximations
papers.summary: The alternating-current optimal power flow (ACOPF) problem is fundamental to power system operation and planning, but its nonconvexity makes globally optimal solutions of large-scale instances computationally challenging. Convex relaxations provide tractable lower bounds for assessing solution quality and supporting global optimization, although their effectiveness depends strongly on relaxation strength. This paper proposes an offline convexification and bound tightening framework for constructing strong linear programming (LP) relaxations for families of related ACOPF instances. Rather than repeating the tightening procedure for each instance, we compute variable bounds and second-order cone outer-approximation (SOC-OA) cuts offline using a demand-slack model and reuse them for subsequent instances with the same topology and admissible demand variations. Computational results on PGLib instances show that the fully offline approach achieves an average gap of $4.32\%$, compared with $3.80\%$ for the fully online approach, while achieving an average speedup of approximately $272\times$. The results demonstrate that offline convexification and bound tightening can recover most of the relaxation improvement of online tightening while significantly reducing the computational burden for repeated ACOPF evaluations.

papers.title: On Exact Critical-Region Boundaries in Continuous-Time Multiparametric Optimal Control Problems
papers.summary: Continuous-time multiparametric model predictive control solves the optimal control problem once, offline, for every initial state, and divides the initial-state space into critical regions, each with its own control law and sequence of active constraints. A boundary between two regions is either a hyperplane, given by one linear equation, or curved. The curved boundaries have not been computed to date; a classifier has been trained instead to distinguish the regions, so the partition has been known only approximately. In this paper we show that a curved boundary can be computed exactly, without solving any optimal control problem. The method rests on one property. Once the sequence of active constraints is fixed, together with the instants inside it at which a constraint becomes active or inactive (the switching times) and the instant at which the change of the neighboring region first appears (the event time), every condition on a boundary is a linear equation in the initial state, so the computation of a boundary, curved or not, is exact. We fix one of these instants, a switching time or the event time, and solve the linear equations that correspond to it for the corresponding initial state on the boundary; stepping the fixed instant along the horizon yields the whole boundary. A hyperplane is the case in which no instant is left to fix. We illustrate the method on the Newell-Lee evaporator, which has seven critical regions and eight boundaries, four hyperplanes and four curved, computing one boundary of each type in full with the adjacent regions at its ends.

papers.title: Incremental-Smoothing-Based ARAIM Protection Levels for Tightly Coupled GNSS/IMU Integration in Urban Canyons
papers.summary: Protection levels (PLs) bound position errors under specified fault hypotheses and risk budgets, but advanced re-ceiver autonomous integrity monitoring (ARAIM) is formulated for snapshot GNSS estimation rather than the correlated poste-rior of tightly coupled GNSS/IMU factor graph optimization (FGO). This paper formulates ARAIM solution separation and PL computation on the FGO posterior. Because current-epoch pseudorange factors enter only the current-state block of the fixed-lag information matrix, the fault-excluded position covari-ance, solution separation, and nominal-bias propagation follow exactly from the linearized current-state marginal, which re-tains correlations with velocity, IMU-bias, and clock states and with historical information. Woodbury updates with selected-output evaluation compute these quantities for fault-free, single-satellite, constellation-wide, and second-order hypotheses with-out repeated full-state inversion or graph re-optimization. Sur-rounding monitoring layers screen measurements, handle post-fit outliers, and determine PL validity and availability. In two road experiments, both nominal sequences achieve 100% hori-zontal and vertical empirical bounding over PL-valid epochs, with a maximum error-to-PL ratio of 0.96. Normalized errors show that the posterior covariance alone does not capture slowly varying ranging biases: a covariance-only bound computed from the same posteriors retains no resolvable margin, and strong temporal correlation limits the empirical evidence to consisten-cy checks rather than validation of the integrity budget. On identical Experiment A posteriors, the proposed method reduces fault-hypothesis evaluation and PL solving time by 65.2% rela-tive to direct full-state inversion with matching integrity deci-sions, and controlled fault injections demonstrate fail-safe PL invalidation while navigation continues.

papers.title: Multi-Timescale Context-Aware Radio Resource Optimization for Harmonious NTN-TN Coexistence: A Digital Twin and Open RAN Enabled Framework
papers.summary: Coexistence between non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) and terrestrial networks (TNs) is essential for future wireless systems, but terrestrial downlink transmissions can generate harmful aggregate interference at low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellite receivers. We present DT-STABLE, an Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN)-enabled, digital twin (DT)-assisted framework for context-aware NTN-TN coexistence. Using site-specific information, the DT estimates interference at LEO satellites, enabling proactive management with reduced real-time measurement overhead. We formulate joint beam activation and user association under RF-chain limits, load balancing, and aggregate satellite interference constraints; prove NP-hardness; and develop an efficient DT-guided scheduling algorithm. DT-STABLE couples short-timescale radio resource adaptation with periodic mid- and long-timescale DT updates through standardized O-RAN interfaces. Site-specific 28 GHz simulations under worst-case satellite geometry and low elevation angles show that DT-STABLE balances rate and interference utility, achieving 89.63% interference-to-noise ratio (INR) satisfaction and a mean sum rate of 210.96 bps/Hz, with nearly 100% INR satisfaction when satellite protection is prioritized. The framework reduces beam measurement overhead by 99.71% relative to exhaustive sweeping and achieves up to 33.1 times lower runtime than the Gurobi-based exact optimization benchmark.

papers.title: Noisy Target Training Meets Drifting for Weakly-Supervised Speech Enhancement
papers.summary: In speech enhancement, standard supervised training requires pairs of noisy and clean speech. Such pairs are typically created by artificially degrading clean speech, leading to a domain mismatch between synthetic training data and real recordings. Noisy target training (NyTT) mitigates this limitation by training an enhancement model to predict a noisy recording from a noisier version generated by adding extra noise. However, since the training target is noisy, NyTT might learn to leave residual noise in the enhanced output. In this paper, we address this issue in NyTT by incorporating a Sinkhorn drifting loss that matches the distribution of the enhanced speech to that of unpaired clean speech. The Sinkhorn drifting loss attracts enhanced speech toward high-density regions of the clean-speech distribution while repelling it from the current enhanced-speech distribution in latent space. This loss uses only unpaired clean speech rather than the clean counterpart of each degraded recording, preserving the weakly-supervised nature of NyTT. Experimental results on VoiceBank-DEMAND and CHiME-3 real recordings demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed combination.

papers.title: Polyhedral RIS Architecture with Quantum-Assisted Facet Selection for Uniform Coverage
papers.summary: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) direct coverage toward moving user equipment (UE), but practical deployments involve discrete phase control, uncertain facet positions, and UE mobility, which require the problem to be re-solved continually. We consider these challenges for the chamfered hexagonal polyhedral RIS, which provides nearly uniform coverage. With both incidence and departure angles, we bound in closed form the gain loss of its best facet relative to the best possible reflecting facet, include the known b-bit quantization loss, and extend the bound to joint random mounting errors of all facets. For a precoded multi-user downlink, each facet-selection subproblem of the max-min rate design is shown to be an exact quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problem, suited to repeated time-constrained solving. The deployment of the base station in relation to the RIS allows the polyhedral surface to bring down the percentage of dead zones in vertical planar panels from 77% to 0.3% and increase the minimum rate by 34% relative to the STAR panel. The simulated annealing algorithm finds the optimum solution in 95% of the cases. The quantum approximation algorithm fails to do so.

papers.title: Time-Varying Kernel Density Deconvolution using Random Finite Set Theory for State Noise Identification
papers.summary: This paper focuses on the noise density identification for state-space models of linear time-varying systems. The density knowledge is essential for the optimal design of any modern state estimator, fault detector, or controller. The proposed method builds on newly derived algorithms for (i) calculation of the measurement prediction residue being independent of the state and linear in state and measurement noises, and (ii) kernel density deconvolution for process with non-stationary statistical properties based on the random finite set theory. The proposed method provides consistent estimate of the state noise density without any prior knowledge on distribution family, which is a unique property in noise identification state-of-the-art. The method is further enhanced by an automatic selection of the user-defined parameters, and is evaluated in numerical examples. The examples demonstrate not only the superior performance of the proposed method in terms of accuracy and robustness among others in ultra-wide-band-inspired tracking scenario, but also the importance of the correct state noise density identification for optimal state estimation and fault detection. The paper is supplemented with a MATLAB implementation.

papers.title: Hierarchical Coherent Imaging of Composite Anisotropic Moving Targets in ISAC
papers.summary: In Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) networks, distributed devices can cooperate to produce radio images of the surrounding environment by exploiting phase-coherent signal processing. However, existing imaging methods are not well-suited for composite moving targets with multiple independently moving extended parts. This is due to simplistic isotropic scattering models and the lack of methods to compensate for distinct Doppler shifts from each component, which leads to image defocusing. We propose MOSAIC, the first hierarchical imaging method for composite moving targets using distributed User Equipments (UEs) and a single ISAC Base Station (BS). MOSAIC generates high-resolution images of each target part and estimates its velocity vector. Coherent imaging is performed within selected clusters of UEs observing a locally isotropic scattering from each part, while cluster-specific images are combined non-coherently across wide angles to improve the reconstruction. To mitigate Doppler-induced defocusing, Doppler components are pre-compensated before coherent imaging, turning a limitation into an additional means of resolving multiple target parts. This also enables low-complexity velocity estimation by associating Doppler frequencies across UEs. Simulations show a 35% to 45% improvement in image quality compared to existing methods, in terms of Wasserstein distance, and dm/s-level velocity estimation accuracy.

papers.title: Accelerating Fractal Image Compression Using Search Pruning and Fractal Dimension Gating
papers.summary: Fractal image compression (FIC) can achieve high compression ratios and fast decoding, but its encoding stage requires an expensive search for matching image blocks. This paper evaluates two implementation strategies for reducing this cost: isometry pruning, and fractal-dimension-based search gating. The gating method uses a box-counting estimate of range-block complexity to determine whether the domain-pool search should be performed. Experiments on the Monkey, Einstein, and Cameraman grayscale images examine two domain/range block-size configurations. The results show that isometry pruning substantially reduces total execution time. Combining isometry pruning with box-counting gating further reduces the number of searched blocks and the bitrate, although the resulting reduction in PSNR depends on the selected thresholds. These findings characterize the trade-off among execution time, bitrate, and reconstruction quality.

papers.title: Computationally Efficient Neural Receiver via Axial Self-Attention
papers.summary: Deep learning-based neural receivers offer promising physical-layer solutions for next-generation wireless systems. We propose an axial self-attention transformer neural receiver that achieves state-of-the-art Block Error Rate (BLER) performance with significantly improved computational efficiency during inference and large-scale training. By factorizing attention operations along temporal and spectral axes, the proposed architecture reduces computational complexity from $O((TF)^2)$ to $O(T^2F+TF^2)$, yielding substantially fewer floating-point operations and attention matrix multiplications per transformer block. Experimental validation under 3GPP Clustered Delay Line (CDL) channels demonstrates consistent performance gains across varying mobility scenarios. Under non-line-of-sight conditions, our proposed axial neural receiver outperforms global self-attention and convolutional neural receiver baselines at 10% BLER and 1% BLER respectively, with reduced computational complexity.
